course:
The course allows us to be creative in our own ways, without restricting us too much. It proveides us a variety of texts, text types, and authors for us to choose from.

On the other hand, it restricts us too much also if you consider the facts that there is a guideline which is so accurate that you know what to say after each sentence almost. Moreover, I don't think that we give enough attention to analyzing, for both when it comes to reading and writing, which makes me question how correlated our course is to the essentials of an academic writing.

Strongest aspect was definitely the discussion topics. Unlike travel blogs, the topics were all about philosophy which fits the idea of this class more where you are forced to display your opinion like a lawyer regardless of it's truth value. As long as you are interested, it makes the topics easier to talk and discuss. May become a weak aspect if you are not interested in philosophy in the slightest. Another strong point would be the in-class activities, it stirs up debates and discussions so you have an easier time connecting with people from different majors.

Weakest aspect is how demanding some courses are and how long the course is. 5 hours a week for this course seemed over the top and the tasks you are working with can be hard. Instructor made it up with how good she is but I can't possibly imagine taking this course through another instructor and having this good of an outcome.
